You can keep buying an extra version of everything each grocery trip until you are satisfied with the size of your food store. Once you are happy with that, you only buy replacements for what you use.

You can't really do milk, fresh fruits, and fresh veggies like this, but you can do most other things. How many of each thing you have will depend on your available storage and how long they stay shelf stable. Using this method, you don't need special survival food or anything. Even most prepackaged snacks stay good for weeks or months or longer, so they will store just fine using this method.

In place of fresh fruit and veggies you can buy some canned fruits and veggies to store. In place of milk, you can buy some dry milk. Those items will stay good for a long time and won't need to be rotated as often. I would also try and store up some cheap, shelf stable items like beans, rice, lentils, etc. If you don't eat them already then I would recommend doing so, but even if you don't they are good to have on hand and store for years at room temperature.
